Is he actually arguing that elevator operator is the only job that has been taken by technology? Oh boy, that is way off. There are hundreds of jobs that no longer exist because of technology. I'm old enough to remember dialing 0 to get the operator. Switchboard operators don't exist anymore. There used to be thousands of women called calculators that did math all day before computers. That position is also completely vanished. Once upon a time when you went bowling there were bowling pin setters (usually boys). The Circle K gas stations in Phoenix, AZ (where I live) don't have cashiers. Neither does Walmart, Target, or grocery stores. Is that I've finished this video I'm trying to figure out what point he was making. If it was that only one job has been replaced by technology then he is not only wrong, but he should have defined his definitions better. When we were children we came home when the street lights turned on, not when the lamp lighters came out to light them. I'm not really sure what the point of this video was. If you are already a working adult I wouldn't worry about your job being taken unless you work in obviously dissappearing fields such as Taxi Driver. I have a daughter in university and despite starting out as an engineering major, she transferred to Video Game Design. Everyone has warned her that AI will be taking that job over the next decade or two. I've told her to get whatever AI certs she can. P. S. The writing, editing, and composition of this video is pro level. Thanks.

In our business AI most definitely is replacing jobs; But the skill vs cost for the business ends were not meeting to begin with. We need very unique level of skill and experience, at a very minimalistic hourly rate, which is impossible cross over to meet in extreme taxation country like Finland. We kept trying to hire for a decade, only to fail one after another hire. Now, "The Position" (and few follow ups) got "filled". The business is FINALLY growing again, at a rampant speed. So did it replace, or simply enable us to grow to the point where we can finally pay the kind of wage to attract the kind of talent we need? You'll be the judge.
